newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS BETTER THAN 1974 AND 1989, SAYS COACH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS BETTER THAN 1974 AND 1989, SAYS COACH.

text.p: British Lions coach Ian McGeechan rates his side's triumph over South Africa as a greater achievement than the series wins posted by the Lions in both 1974 and 1989.

The shrewd Scots tactician, sporting a crewcut courtesy of Irish hooker Keith Wood after promising his players in London that he would have a haircut if they won the first two tests, was part of all three Lions' successes as either player or coach.

McGeechan, who played in the centre for Willie John McBride's 1974 team and later inspired the 1989 tourists to bounce back from an opening test defeat to beat Australia 2-1, said the 1997 Lions experience was the most satisfying.
"It's always difficult to compare historically but I would say this is probably the most satisfying of all of them simply because of the massive challenge we had," McGeechan said.

"And that's all because of the season we'd at home, coming into it as we were and the high quality games that we had to play right through. I would say, quite comfortably as far I'm concerned, this is the biggest one in recent history I've been involved in."
McGeechan said a special bonus of the Lions' 18-15 win in Durban on Saturday was that it had been achieved with 15-man rugby.
"That was the great advantage -- that we won it with 15-man rugby when we just didn't have the ball half the time.

"With this squad there has been a 15-man commitment to the game and a common ability to slot into areas where the players weren't necessarily familiar. The whole thing allows you a more complete picture of what you can do, whether you have the all or not."
While McGeechan admitted the Lions made several mistakes during the second test, he was impressed by his team's rugby during the final quarter.
"We gave the ball away, particularly in the first half. But we weathered the storm and we were never more than a score away from them.

"In the last 15 minutes I thought we played quite cleverly, we manufactured positions. Neil Jenkins again had an outstanding game with his goal-kicking and, when we got the opportunities, we made the most of them."
"You just don't get Five Nations matches like yesterday's game where you get so many questions asked so often," said McGeechan.

"But these players will now be better for what they've experienced in the last two games. They've been playing rugby they've never been asked to play -- by Jim Telfer and myself and by their opponents."
